review_only_corrections: 125 currently readable Murata primary source instead of redirected Schaffner PDF

records.rationale: Correct non-exhaustive mains-filter component inventory and distinction between noise paths. X and Y capacitor placement and common-mode choke use are conventional; no component rating, leakage limit or complete certified filter design is invented.

evidence.title: Murata power-line common-mode chokes
evidence.finding: AC mains filtering uses a common-mode choke, X capacitors and Y capacitors to address different common-mode and differential-mode paths.

records.rationale: Defines calibration as adjustment, conflating two distinct metrological operations. Calibration establishes the reference-to-indication relationship and its uncertainty and can be performed without altering the sensor. Offset/gain adjustment may follow calibration but is not its definition.

evidence.title: BIPM/JCGM VIM calibration definition
evidence.finding: Calibration establishes relationships between reference quantity values and indications with uncertainty; adjustment is a distinct operation.

records.rationale: Appropriate evidence-gathering checklist for an early relay failure, distinguishing electrical erosion, mechanical wear and contamination/misapplication instead of diagnosing from cycle count alone. It does not assign an unsupported failure cause or service-life guarantee.

evidence.title: OMRON relay troubleshooting
evidence.finding: Mechanical relays have multiple failure mechanisms, including contact welding, wear, intermittent contact and coil deterioration.

records.rationale: Reasonable conditional practical answer: a user may compare a sensor with a suitable known reference and perform permissible offset/gain adjustment, while the required accuracy affects reference quality. It does not define calibration as synonymous with adjustment or claim accreditation/traceability for an unspecified home method.

evidence.title: BIPM/JCGM VIM calibration definition
evidence.finding: Calibration establishes relationships between reference quantity values and indications with uncertainty; adjustment is a distinct operation.

records.rationale: Correct conditional warning for triac-based AC SSRs on a DC motor: removing the input may not commutate the output off. It does not infer the internal topology solely from a voltage label because it explicitly says if it is a triac AC SSR.

evidence.title: OMRON AC SSR on DC load
evidence.finding: Triac/thyristor AC output stages need load-current commutation and may remain on under DC load despite removing the input signal.

records.rationale: The claim that every signal below the noise floor disappears regardless of ADC resolution is too absolute. Detectability depends on measurement bandwidth, integration time and signal structure; averaging or phase-sensitive detection can recover signals below broadband noise. ADC resolution alone is insufficient, but that does not justify an immutable detection cutoff.

evidence.title: Stanford Research Systems lock-in principles
evidence.finding: Phase-sensitive detection and narrow measurement bandwidth can recover signals below broadband noise.

For independent zero-mean noise of standard deviation sigma, averaging N samples reduces mean noise to sigma/sqrt(N) while retaining a constant signal. At N=100 the noise standard deviation is one tenth of its single-sample value.

records.rationale: Correct practical warning that a magnetometer senses the net local field rather than tagging Earth's contribution and that nearby magnetic disturbances can spoil heading. Calibration or an alternative approach is appropriately presented rather than a guarantee that calibration removes arbitrary changing fields.

evidence.title: Analog Devices hard/soft-iron correction
evidence.finding: Local magnetic fields/materials perturb magnetometer observations and can require calibration or another heading strategy.

records.rationale: Correctly makes drop survival dependent on the actual shock rating and recognizes possible structural damage or calibration shift. The answer does not certify a drop height from a peak-g value or equate measurement full-scale range with shock survivability.

evidence.title: Analog Devices MEMS shock limits
evidence.finding: Shock survival limits are device-specific and can be exceeded during drops or board processing.

evidence.title: Analog Devices shock and vibration distinction
evidence.finding: Shock ratings include amplitude, duration and waveform; vibration tolerance is a separate repetitive mechanical condition.

records.rationale: Sound qualitative warning that unqualified vibration exposure increases risk of interconnect, solder and mechanical failures. It provides examples of mechanisms, not a quantified probability or a claim that simply omitting a paperwork check physically causes failure.

evidence.title: Analog Devices shock and vibration distinction
evidence.finding: Shock ratings include amplitude, duration and waveform; vibration tolerance is a separate repetitive mechanical condition.

evidence.title: OMRON relay troubleshooting
evidence.finding: Mechanical relays have multiple failure mechanisms, including contact welding, wear, intermittent contact and coil deterioration.

records.rationale: Caution about weak extrapolation and checking mechanisms/models is sound, but the prompt supplies no observed life trend or statistical evidence for stress dependence. A weak Arrhenius fit at three stress levels does not establish that tested life probably changes with stress. Hold that initial inference; the rest of the reporting guidance remains useful.

evidence.title: NIST accelerated life tests
evidence.finding: Use-condition life projection requires an appropriate failure mechanism and acceleration/life models; stress selection and sampling affect model quality.
A noisy dataset with equal underlying lifetime distributions at all three stress levels can also yield a weak Arrhenius fit. The stated fit quality alone does not identify a stress effect.

records.rationale: Slow sensing can lose fast dynamics and add destabilizing loop phase lag. However, filtering the process downstream is not a specified remedy for missing sensor bandwidth and may add still more lag. The answer needs a defined control-bandwidth/compensation change or explicit willingness to abandon fast-response requirements rather than a vague filtering fix.

evidence.finding: A first-order sensor H(s)=1/(1+s*tau) attenuates high frequencies and adds phase lag. Cascading another ordinary low-pass filter cannot restore those lost dynamics and adds further phase lag.

records.rationale: Correct concise freewheel-diode purpose: maintain a path for inductive current after the switch opens and limit the otherwise large voltage. Circulating stored energy is conventional shorthand for recirculating current while energy dissipates; no ideal lossless perpetual circulation or universal release time is claimed.

evidence.title: TI solenoid driving topologies
evidence.finding: Discusses low-side/high-side and bridge switching, recirculation and clamp choices for inductive solenoid loads.
Inductor current cannot change instantaneously; a correctly oriented diode closes a current path and clamps the switching node, while coil/diode losses dissipate the stored 0.5*L*I².

records.rationale: Correctly separates signal-voltage compatibility from galvanic separation. The answer explicitly permits an interface to do both and does not claim that all level shifters isolate or that any isolated component automatically meets a particular safety standard.

evidence.title: TI isolation technology comparison
evidence.finding: Optocoupler delay/CTR/aging and CMTI are device-dependent; integrated isolator solutions can also be cost-effective rather than universally more expensive.

records.rationale: The straight-line definition is broadly correct, but doubling raw output when input doubles requires zero intercept. Linear sensor transfer curves can have nonzero offset; the answer silently conflates a straight-line/affine calibration relationship with direct proportionality.

evidence.title: Analog Devices TMP36 linear sensor
evidence.finding: TMP36 has a linear 10 mV/degree-C transfer with 750 mV at 25 degrees C, hence a nonzero offset; linearity does not require the raw output to double with temperature.
For y=a*x+b, y(2x)=2*a*x+b, while 2*y(x)=2*a*x+2*b. Equality requires b=0. A TMP36-type ideal line gives 0.75 V at 25 C and 1.00 V at 50 C, not 1.50 V.

records.rationale: Correct basic PWM low-side switching principle for a suitable DC motor: changing duty cycle changes the applied average terminal voltage. It is a one-sentence functional description, not a complete gate-drive, recirculation, current-limit or installation design.

evidence.title: TI solenoid driving topologies
evidence.finding: Discusses low-side/high-side and bridge switching, recirculation and clamp choices for inductive solenoid loads.
For ideal pulses between zero and supply voltage, average voltage over a cycle is D*Vs; real freewheel/switch drops and motor dynamics modify the detailed relationship.

records.rationale: Accurate broad definition of power integrity and its power-distribution-network concerns, including impedance, decoupling and transient/regulator behavior. Behave like an ideal source states a design objective within relevant bandwidth rather than asserting physically zero impedance at all frequencies.

evidence.title: Analog Devices grounding guidance
evidence.finding: Local bypassing and controlled low-impedance current paths help keep switching currents from contaminating ADC circuitry; topology and frequency matter.

records.rationale: Appropriately declines to infer reliability from one failure and an unspecified 500-hour exposure. Sample size, exposure/mission definition, confidence and failure mechanism are essential; the answer computes no unjustified MTBF or reliability probability.

evidence.title: NIST accelerated life tests
evidence.finding: Use-condition life projection requires an appropriate failure mechanism and acceleration/life models; stress selection and sampling affect model quality.
One event count without defined total unit-hours and a model does not identify a mission reliability function or a defensible confidence bound.

records.rationale: Correct functional distinction between ordinary overload/short-circuit breakers and dedicated arc-signature detection. The concise standard-breakers-don't wording concerns arc-fault protection functionality, not a claim that a conventional breaker can never open during an arc that also causes sufficient overcurrent.

evidence.title: CPSC AFCI safety explanation
evidence.finding: AFCIs detect arcing characteristics that ordinary overload/short-circuit protection is not designed to recognize.

evidence.title: CPSC AFCI information sheet
evidence.finding: AFCIs detect dangerous arcing that conventional overcurrent protection may not detect.

records.rationale: Encoder, Hall and back-EMF options are reasonable, and an analog tachogenerator is one tachometer implementation. But encoders are the most common in modern designs is an unsupported prevalence ranking without a motor/application population, and tachometer is not universally an analog-voltage device. Hold these generic overstatements rather than choosing a sensor for the unspecified motor.

evidence.title: TI motor-control speed observers
evidence.finding: Encoder, Hall and sensorless observer approaches are available; this establishes options rather than an industry-wide prevalence ranking.

records.rationale: Plane-pair cavity resonance is a sound mechanism, but breaking up uniform planes is offered as a general mitigation without stack-up or return-path constraints. Unplanned splits can increase return inductance and EMI. The remedy needs topology-specific qualification rather than treating arbitrary fragmentation as a safe resonance cure.

evidence.title: Analog Devices AN-1142 layout guidance
evidence.finding: Blindly splitting a reference plane can increase return-path inductance and noise; a topology-specific reason and controlled return path are required.
Altering boundaries changes resonant modes but does not guarantee lower impedance at every relevant frequency; a split can force a signal return loop to take a longer path.

records.rationale: Reasonable conditional preference for a suitably driven MOSFET in a battery-powered pulsed DC solenoid application, considering low steady gate power and BJT base/saturation loss. It explicitly leaves voltage/current/pulse/topology and special-release requirements open rather than selecting an unspecified part.

evidence.title: TI solenoid driving topologies
evidence.finding: Discusses low-side/high-side and bridge switching, recirculation and clamp choices for inductive solenoid loads.

records.rationale: Correct definition and example of unintended sensitivity to another physical quantity. It distinguishes cross-sensitivity from the intended measurand without asserting a magnitude or requiring zero secondary response in every real sensor.

evidence.finding: If pressure-sensor output y(P,T) has nonzero partial derivative with respect to T at fixed P, temperature affects the output independently of the intended pressure measurement.

records.rationale: LED aging, CTR spread and speed/delay trade-offs are real, but high common-mode-transient handling and modern isolators cost more are unqualified class-wide comparisons. CMTI and total solution cost depend on actual parts and circuit requirements; the prompt provides none. Hold those overgeneralizations while retaining the valid trade-off discussion.

evidence.title: TI isolation technology comparison
evidence.finding: Optocoupler delay/CTR/aging and CMTI are device-dependent; integrated isolator solutions can also be cost-effective rather than universally more expensive.

records.rationale: Declares welded contacts and a prior arc event as the certain cause from a failure-to-drop-out symptom. Manufacturer troubleshooting lists other mechanisms such as residual magnetism or mechanical problems. The absolute only-way-to-stop statement and replacement diagnosis are therefore not justified by the visible information, although safely isolating power is sensible for a runaway load.

evidence.title: Schneider motor-control troubleshooting
evidence.finding: Failure to drop out has multiple causes, including residual magnetism and welded contacts; the symptom alone does not identify a unique mechanism.
The same observed no-dropout symptom can arise from at least two documented causes, so it cannot uniquely prove contact welding.

records.rationale: Correct practical link between transformer regulation, winding/leakage impedance, no-load voltage and rectifier/regulator margins. Usually and might appropriately avoid an absolute claim for all power factors or transformer designs. It supplies no unsupported numeric rating or capacitor/regulator selection.

evidence.title: Hammond transformer regulation examples
evidence.finding: Transformer rated secondary voltages/current and regulation vary by design, supporting the need to account for load-dependent output voltage.

A secondary-equivalent source behind series R+jX has load-dependent terminal voltage. A capacitor-input rectifier can approach sqrt(2)*Vrms at light load, while loaded droop/ripple reduce regulator headroom.
